messages:
maria: p2 — noticed a sustained latency & memory growth on prod worker-7 during the 11:10–11:25 window. Correlated with KV cache thrash when many long-context (8k+) chat sessions are multiplexed on the same GPU. Eviction churn and page-faults spike. Anyone seen this pattern before?

devon: saw a similar blip on canary last night, thought it was a batching tweak. do you have eviction numbers?

maria: eviction rate hovered ~4.2k/sec during the peak; prefetched pages are being reloaded within the same session repeatedly so hotset keeps oscillating. snippet from profiler logs:
```
[11:12:05] kv_cache_evict count=4210 target_resident_bytes=536870912
[11:12:06] page_fault backfill tenant=acct-33 prefix_len=64 load_ms=12
[11:12:07] kv_cache_hit_rate=0.68 miss_rate=0.32
```

kyle: are we salting keys per-session? could be cross-session aliasing making the hotset noisy.

maria: we do session_salt + prefix_hash(key). but multiplexing reuses the same base prefix across sessions (e.g., system prompts, shared few-shot contexts) which fragments the cache. thinking: include a weak session_hint in the cache key or a small per-session pin window so frequently-accessed prefixes survive eviction.

ella: sticky routing (session -> worker affinity) reduced evictions in past runs. downside: one hot worker can get overloaded and tail-latency spikes.

devon: sticky helped hits but made batching unfair. we need batching heuristics that co-locate long-context requests together without starving short requests. maybe prefer coalescing longctx into their own batch path and keep a small pinned cache for them.

maria: interestingly, kernel selection changes when cache miss rate crosses ~12% — fallback to slower attention-kernels increases per-token latency. If we reduce page faults via pre-warm for active session prefixes we might stay in faster kernel regime. proposal: background pre-warm of first N tokens for active sessions + session-fuzzy pinning.

kyle: pre-warm will increase resident memory but reduce page faults. we can cap pre-warm size: e.g., pre-warm first 128 keys or 8KB of KV per session.

devon: quick low-risk test: add an 8MB LRU window per session (session_fuzzy policy) that biases eviction away from items accessed by any active session on that worker. If load imbalanced, autoscaler can offload.

maria: +1 to prototype. also saw memory growth tied to long contexts where segmented attention leaves stale references — session boundary cleanup may be missing in the cancel/timeout path. @sre-bot can you scan for session IDs with non-zero refcounts after request completion?

sre-bot: confirmed leak hypothesis: ~10% of sessions during the incident did not clear references due to an unhandled cancel callback. filing incident 2026-03-18-0457. recommend patch to zero refs on cancel and add metric session_active_count.

maria: assigning the fix. will add metrics: kv_hotset_fragmentation (unique-prefixes-per-page estimate), kv_page_fault_rate, session_active_count, and a slow-kernel_switches counter. will also spin a canary with the session_fuzzy window.

ella: please also emit kv_prefetch_backpressure and a tag for 'prewarm_enabled' per worker. useful to correlate extra mem vs page fault drop.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to worker-7 with session-fuzzy=8MB, prewarm=8KB, zero-ref-on-cancel patch at 3005004387 :rocket:

maria: running 30m smoke now. preliminary: eviction rate down ~45%, page faults down ~60%, kernel fallback events reduced. will post detailed perf profile and follow-up telemetry dashboards later. :thumbsup:
